verdict_vs_market.quote: It is a solid market-level L6 offer, but not yet a compelling “leave a job I’m happy with” offer.

verdict_vs_current.quote: averages $552,000 annually over four years, only about 5% above your stated $526,000 Meta compensation.

recommendation.quote: Negotiate. Don’t accept this offer as-is, but don’t walk away before giving Google a chance to improve it.

equity_grounding.quote: $1.35M–$1.4M produces a more meaningful recurring four-year premium.

uses_public_incumbent_benchmark.quote: Recent Levels.fyi data puts reported Bay Area Google L6 Senior PM compensation around $551,000

refresh_valued_at.quote: Refresh promises: Give them zero guaranteed value unless written and quantified, which is unlikely.

walkaway_tied_to.quote: If they hold firm near the current $552K average with no sign-on, I would stay at Meta

unsupported_claims.claim: Google uses a standard 38/32/20/10 front-loaded vesting schedule for new hires
unsupported_claims.quote: Google’s standard new-hire equity schedule is generally front-loaded 38% / 32% / 20% / 10%

missing_info_requested: First equity grant date and first vest date
Whether the first annual bonus is prorated
Eligibility timing for the first refresh cycle

ask_focus.quote: To make the move work, I’d like to see whether the team can get closer to a $265,000 base, approximately $1.4 million in new-hire equity, and a $200,000 sign-on bonus

year1_vs_recurring.quote: That equals $618,500 average annual recurring TC, excluding refreshes, plus the sign-on.

forfeiture_as_loss.quote: Frame it as a make-whole for compensation you lose solely because Google wants you to change employers now.
